quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — Q3 2026 GUIDANCE AND YEAR FRAMEWORK, CFO David Zinsner: 'we're guiding Q3 revenue to a range of $15.8 billion-$16.8 billion. At the midpoint of $16.3 billion, we forecast gross margin of 42%, a tax rate of 11%, and EPS of $0.38, all on a non-GAAP basis.' Non-GAAP operating expenses held to 'roughly $16.5 billion for the year'. Supply growth is 'more skewed towards the end of Q3 and into Q4, especially for servers'. Q3 by segment: client revenue 'kind of flattish', CCPG 'likely to be up a bit' on edge growth; the PC market is expected 'down in the quarter', and Intel 'likely would see some build in CPUs for Q3' at customers. Gross margin guided flat QoQ: no repeat of the Q2 inventory write-down, offset by Panther Lake and Granite still below the corporate average early in their life cycle; the year's goal is 'to get gross margins comfortably into the 40%s in every quarter'. Longer term, gross-margin fall-through 'somewhere in the 40%-60% range'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 guide $15.8B-$16.8B (midpoint $16.3B); non-GAAP GM 42%, tax 11%, EPS $0.38; FY non-GAAP opex ~$16.5B

quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — CLIENT AND EDGE (CCPG), CFO: CCPG revenue $8.9 billion, up 15% sequentially; AI PC revenue grew 26% sequentially; edge deployments roughly 10% of CCPG revenue. CCPG operating profit $2.3 billion, 26% of revenue, down approximately $173 million QoQ on inventory charges — products not fully completed 'from a match set perspective' were written down as 'somewhat stranded inventory'. Client brought 18A to full scale with 400+ designs for Series 3; 40+ Arc integrated graphics designs; introduced Intel Arc G-Series processors for handheld gaming systems; vPro manageability activations 'surged 1,500% over the last four quarters'; 130 Series 3 design wins for edge AI applications, including robotics. CFO: the edge and physical AI opportunity 'is likely to at least match the client TAM over time'. Client strength was 'largely ASP', partly mix and partly like-for-like price increases passing on cost inflation; Intel will 'pivot as much of the production as possible over to CPUs and data centers'.
quarterly_data.figure: CCPG $8.9B (+15% QoQ); AI PC +26% QoQ; CCPG op profit $2.3B (26%), -$173M QoQ on inventory charges; 400+ Series 3 designs; 130 edge AI design wins; vPro activations +1,500%

quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — DATA CENTER (DCAI) AND THE SERVER ROADMAP: CFO: DCAI revenue $6.3 billion, 'an increase of 24% sequentially and 59% year-over-year', driven by hyperscale and enterprise; Xeon 6+ is codenamed Clearwater Forest; 'all of our server wafers are procured internally for the most part. Some of the ASIC stuff isn't'; Granite Rapids on Intel 3 is 'extremely tight', with 'a pretty good ramp of Intel 3 planned for the rest of this year and next year'; 'Our outlook for server CPU demand has improved again since our last earnings report'. CEO Lip-Bu Tan: 'additional strategic customer wins and long-term agreements in Q2'; the data-center roadmap is 'Clearwater Forest, Diamond Rapids, and also Coral Rapids', with multithreading 'coming in the Coral Rapids'; 'Some areas we are still behind, but we are catching up very fast'. On Arm (CEO): 'Arm is a great partner for us' and 'They can be a great partner and customer, especially in the IP front.' CFO: 'particularly in places where we've gotten long-term agreements', Intel now has the signal to forecast demand for the next few years.
quarterly_data.figure: DCAI $6.3B (+24% QoQ, +59% YoY); roadmap Clearwater Forest -> Diamond Rapids -> Coral Rapids (SMT)

quarterly_data.signal: CALL (verbatim) — INDUSTRY SUPPLY AND INTEL'S STRATEGIC VIEW: CEO Lip-Bu Tan: 'Industry is facing one of the most severe supply constraints in its history across leading-edge logic, silicon wafers, memory, and substrates. These shortages will persist for the foreseeable future.' CFO: 'Industry-wide supply constraints across wafers, memory, and substrates remain the dominant challenge our customers are facing'; Intel is 'aggressively locking in tool purchase orders from our vendors, accelerating our clean room build-outs, and actively securing supply of substrates and memory.' CFO: 'Emerging markets in physical AI, purpose-built silicon, advanced packaging, and external wafers are each multibillion-dollar annual revenue opportunities for us in the not-too-distant future.' CEO (company claim): 'We are the only company that can design, manufacturing, build the entire range of computing solutions from general purpose, traditional CPUs and GPUs, to more purpose-built ASICs and CPUs optimized for agentic AI.'

CALL (verbatim) — FOUNDRY NODES, TOOLING AND THE CAPEX DISCIPLINE: CFO: Intel Foundry revenue $5.8 billion, 'up 6% sequentially on higher fab volumes driven by strong growth in Intel 18A'. CEO Lip-Bu Tan: factories across Intel 7, Intel 3 and Intel 18A 'exceeded internal volume targets'; 18A-P 'is in the risk production now. That will be ready before the end of this year', with 'a 5% enhanced performance'; Intel continues to 'build out and validate the IP portfolio for 14A'. CFO on 2026 capex: space is largely in place ('we are in a very good place in terms of space'); 'We'll increase tooling in 2026 by 40% relative to 2025', on 'Intel 3, it's 18A, it'll be 18A-P'; the 2027 number needs 'another quarter or two to really solidify'. The investment-tax-credit gross-to-net is 'running in the kind of low single-digit billions right now'. Back-end investments, 'particularly with third parties', 'could be a drag to cash flow, next year'. CEO: 'I don't put CapEx unless I see the yield performance, the IP is ready to serve the customer, and also customer engagement'; CFO: 'until we really know that we've got the customers, we don't want to put significant amount of capital' — 'we must have pretty significant confidence in our customers, or we wouldn't be putting the POs in place today.'
quarterly_data.figure: Foundry $5.8B (+6% QoQ); 18A-P ready before year-end, 5% performance gain; 2026 tooling +40% vs 2025; ITC gross-to-net low single-digit billions
